authorReview.scope: Complete eight-sentence script checked against canonical short-reader opening evidence for premise, clear identity, specific interest and protected revelations.
authorReview.targetDuration: About one minute at an unhurried conversational pace with real pauses; measure after recording.
authorReview.emotion: Concrete recognition, thoughtful tension and open curiosity; no melodramatic mystery or inflated promise.
authorReview.audioConversion: Blocked until all batch scripts pass independent editorial review.
authorReview.visualExecution: The existing art is preserved as working material; book-specific changes above still require implementation before film validation.

independentReview.notes: Every spoken sentence reviewed against canonical English short reader for clear newcomer meaning, source grounding, curiosity and emotional intent. Replaced abstract promotional commentary with concrete viewer-facing language. All eight sentences have a distinct intended response and explicit restrained TTS direction; fictional later outcomes remain withheld. This is editorial review, not audience testing or rendered-audio approval.

sentenceIntentions.text: An AI’s most consequential sentence may be the verdict you never see.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Make an unseen verdict potentially consequential
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Feel curiosity about decisions behind the visible answer

sentenceIntentions.text: Judgment Engines examines AI systems that grade, rank, approve, and decide what happens next.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Name models acting as graders and gatekeepers
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Understand the book concerns evaluation as control

sentenceIntentions.text: A score can block a software release or influence which work receives serious attention.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Give release and attention as concrete consequences
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Recognize how a small score changes access

sentenceIntentions.text: That changes the stakes when an evaluator mistakes polished language for a better result.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Connect polished language with evaluator error
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Question whether apparent quality influences authority

sentenceIntentions.text: The book follows machine judgment from the rules and evidence it uses into the systems built around it.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Trace judgment from criteria into surrounding systems

sentenceIntentions.text: Its examples connect code, schools, hiring, and science, where a score can become a form of power.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Show the inquiry across code, education and hiring

sentenceIntentions.text: For builders and readers affected by automated decisions, the question is who evaluates the evaluator.
Start with the quiet shift from generation to judgment, and follow the consequences of a score.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Point to generation giving way to judgment
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Want to follow what a score permits or blocks
